documents.title: Syllabus Minimum Requirements Policy (Artificial Intelligence (AI) Usage section)
documents.summary: The Syllabus Minimum Requirements Policy lists what every OSU course syllabus must contain. Its AI section, added by Faculty Senate on 06/11/2026, makes an AI usage policy compulsory but leaves permit or prohibit to the instructor. The rest of the page (course content, Core Education, WIC, disability statements) is unrelated to AI.
documents.stance_why: The policy sets no AI rule itself. It requires every syllabus to carry an AI usage policy and says "Determination of permitted or prohibited AI use remains at the discretion of the instructor", so the decision is handed to instructors.

units.why: This is a syllabus requirement addressed to course syllabi: 'All course syllabi must include an AI usage policy'. It is a P09 type rule because it mandates an AI statement in every syllabus, binds instructors, and is a before-course design duty.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on unit_stance: A=require, B=neutral. The unit requires a syllabus statement; it takes no position on whether students may use AI (the decision is left to the instructor), so the unit stance is neutral. 'require' is reserved for work that requires AI use itself.
units.anchor: must include an AI usage policy that communicates expectations for student use of artificial intelligence

units.why: The sentence 'Determination of permitted or prohibited AI use remains at the discretion of the instructor' says the permit or prohibit decision belongs to each instructor, which is P04 (let each instructor set the rule). It informs rather than commands.
units.anchor: Determination of permitted or prohibited AI use remains at the discretion of the instructor.

documents.title: University Guidance on the Use of Generative AI in Teaching and Learning (memo to faculty)
documents.summary: A September 2025 memo from the Senior Vice Provost introducing university guidance on generative AI in teaching. It names shared commitments, strongly encourages instructors to adopt the guidance and a syllabus statement for fall 2025, announces that a statement will likely become a requirement, and lists workshops and consultations.
documents.stance_why: The memo only "strongly encourage[s]" instructors to follow the guidance and add a GenAI syllabus statement "tailoring it with details of the specific approach", and speaks of "faculty autonomy". It sets no ban or permission itself, so the decision stays with instructors.

units.why: The memo says the guidance reflects 'shared commitments to human cognition and creativity, academic integrity, and inclusive excellence', which states the principles behind the university framework. It is P56 because it is an institution-level preamble, and it informs rather than directs.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on actor: A=all, B=admin. The sentence states shared commitments that the guidance reflects. It is a principle that binds no single role, so the actor is all.
units.anchor: shared commitments to human cognition and creativity, academic integrity, and inclusive excellence
units.frag_end: security of individual and institutional data.

documents.summary: Section 2.21 of the 2025-2026 EECS Graduate Handbook (ECE, CS, AI programs) on AI writing assistance, citation and attribution. It permits AI polishing of the student's own finished content, bans AI-created content or research, warns about plagiarism and self-plagiarism, and requires a similarity check (Draft Coach) on documents submitted to examination committees.
